capitals.name: Braunsberg (Braniewo)
capitals.note: 'in 1251 Anselm of Meissen entered the see of Warmia, which resided at Braunsberg (Braniewo)'. 1243-1250 is a bridge: the page names no seat before Anselm (no bishop in residence), and the first known seat is applied back to the founding so that the state has a capital from its birth.

capitals.name: Frauenburg (Frombork)
capitals.note: The seat 'moved to Frauenburg (Frombork) in 1280 after attacks by heathen Old Prussians'. From 1306 Frauenburg stays the cathedral see (chapter) only; the bishops' seat and the capital is Lidzbark Warmiński.

capitals.name: Lidzbark Warmiński (Heilsberg)
capitals.note: Lidzbark page: 'In 1306 it became the seat for the Bishopric of Warmia, and remained the Prince-Bishop's seat for 500 years' and 'the capital of the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia'; the castle of the Warmian bishops was built in the 1350s. The Prince-Bishopric page's infobox 'Capital: Lidzbark Warmiński' has no year (and wrong coordinates, 53°47'N 20°3'E). The Lidzbark page has the seat until the last prince-bishop's death in 1795; the state ends 1772.

correction.text: Warmia, the bishop's secular third of the diocese (Braniewo, Frombork, Orneta, Lidzbark Warmiński, Reszel, Barczewo, Olsztyn), about 4,500 km2 on the Warmia page

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Teutonic Order and Kingdom of Poland shapes cover the area). 'It was founded as the Bishopric of Ermland by William of Modena in 1243'; the Golden Bull of 1356 confirmed 'The bishop ruled one-third of the bishopric as a secular ruler'. Redrawn after review: the gazetteer region 'Warmia' resolves to 12,645 km2 (the whole Warmian-Masurian voivodeship in a 19.3-21.3 E, 53.6-54.5 N box), which takes in Elbląg and the Ducal Prussian towns Ostróda, Pasłęk, Morąg and Bartoszyce, and the first note wrongly called it 'about 4,000-5,000 km2'. The Warmia article gives 'an area of around 4,500 km2' (the Prince-Bishopric page gives none) and the Pasłęka river as the western border, Olsztyn and Lidzbark Warmiński on the Łyna, Barczewo, Reszel and Orneta as Warmian towns. The shape is now the Warmian-Masurian voivodeship cut by an 11-point polygon through Braniewo, Frombork, Orneta, Lidzbark Warmiński, Reszel, Barczewo and Olsztyn: 5,060 km2 on the grid (20 cells of 253 km2; ratio 1.12 to the page; the grid cannot come nearer than one cell). Disc tests: Braniewo, Frombork, Orneta, Lidzbark, Reszel, Barczewo, Olsztyn and Biskupiec inside; Elbląg, Pasłęk, Morąg, Ostróda and Bartoszyce outside. The Royal Prussia dossier draws Elbląg and leaves this shape out (no overlap on the grid). The gazetteer region 'Warmia' is about 2.8 times too large and should be redrawn.

ledger.note: 1243: William of Modena founds the Bishopric of Ermland in Prussia. 'It was founded as the Bishopric of Ermland by William of Modena in 1243'; the see resided at Braunsberg from 1251 (Anselm of Meissen) and the cathedral chapter 'constituted in 1260'. Counterpart changed from old-prussians after review: the page makes the see 'a protectorate of the Monastic state of the Teutonic Knights (1243-1464)'; old-prussians books the land as theirs until 1253 and teutonic-order books Warmia in 1249, so the founding is the page's date for the diocese and the territorial hold follows the Order's conquest.

ledger.note: 20 September 1260: 'The major revolt began on 20 September 1260' (Great Prussian Uprising); the Warmians under Glappe rose, and 'the rebel headquarters' were at Heilsberg (Lidzbark), in the bishop's domain. The Prince-Bishopric page does not mention the uprising; booking Warmia as contested is my reading, matching old-prussians /ledger/9-10.

ledger.note: 1274: 'the uprising was ended in 1274' with the capture of Heilsberg; 'Natangians and Warmians had also accepted baptism and promised their loyalty to the Knights' by 1277 (old-prussians books the end in 1277).
1280: the seat moves from Braunsberg to Frauenburg (Frombork) 'after attacks by heathen Old Prussians'. A later move to Lidzbark Warmiński follows in 1306.
1306: Lidzbark Warmiński 'became the seat for the Bishopric of Warmia, and remained the Prince-Bishop's seat for 500 years'; Frauenburg remains the cathedral see.
July 1626: after landing at Pillau on 6 July 1626 the Swedes 'rapidly occupied Braniewo, Frombork, Elbląg, Orneta, and Malbork'.
July 1626: Orneta occupied in the same sweep.
September 1629: the truce left Sweden 'the towns of Braunsberg, Frauenberg, and Elbing' in Royal Prussia; Orneta is not on that list, so it returns (my reading).
12 September 1635: the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf 'returned these gains' and Sweden withdrew from Prussia (the Stuhmsdorf page names only Elbing, Memel and Pillau).

wars.outcome: The revolt began on 20 September 1260; the Knights captured the rebel headquarters at Heilsberg in 1274, 'the uprising was ended in 1274', and the Warmians accepted baptism and loyalty by 1277.
wars.note: The page does not say the bishopric was attacked; the see left Braunsberg for Frauenburg in 1280 'after attacks by heathen Old Prussians' (Prince-Bishopric page).

wars.outcome: The Warmian nobility and towns joined the Prussian Confederation (1440); the king signed the act of incorporation on 6 March 1454; the bishopric sided with Poland in 1464; the Peace of Thorn of 1466 had the Order renounce claims.

wars.outcome: A conflict 'over the right to name and approve Bishops in Warmia'; the Polish king accepted Tüngen as prince-bishop at the First Treaty of Piotrków.
wars.note: The page dates the war 1467-1479 and does not date the treaty; the two sides are my reading of the Peace of Thorn page's sentence.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1626-1629)
wars.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus landed at Pillau on 6 July 1626 and took Braniewo, Frombork and Orneta; Sweden retained Braunsberg and Frauenberg under the 1629 truce until the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf (12 September 1635).

certainty.note: The frontier with the Old Prussians and the Order's land was being settled by conquest and partition; the 1260-1274 uprising contested it.
The Golden Bull of 1356 confirmed the bishop's one third of the diocese as a secular domain; the page gives no survey, and the drawn polygon is a stand-in cut to the Warmia page's 4,500 km2.

notes:
Prince-Bishopric of Warmia is a state Cliopatria lacks (flagged by eu-14-f, eu-14-x and eu-15-i). Its secular domain is the one third of the diocese the bishop ruled. The Royal Prussia page counts it in the former territory of Royal Prussia and the Peace of Thorn page says it 'was recognized as part of Poland' in 1466; the royal-prussia dossier leaves it out, so the colour agent should draw Warmia as a client of the Order (to 1464) and of the Polish crown (1464-1772), inside the Royal Prussia area.

Repaired after the review (2026-10-31): (1) Shape redrawn to 5,060 km2 on the grid (Warmia page: around 4,500 km2); the old note's '4,000-5,000 km2' was false because the gazetteer region 'Warmia' is 12,645 km2. The gazetteer agent should shrink 'Warmia'. (2) Capitals: Braunsberg 1243-1279 (1243-1250 a bridge), Frauenburg 1280-1305, Lidzbark Warmiński 1306-1772 (Lidzbark page; the Prince-Bishopric infobox gives it as capital without years); Frauenburg stays the cathedral see. (3) The 1243 counterpart is teutonic-order (the page's protector) instead of old-prussians; the Great Prussian Uprising (20 September 1260 to 1274) is booked as a contest with old-prussians (my reading: the page on the uprising does not mention the bishopric; the Warmians rose and Heilsberg was the rebel headquarters). The old-prussians dossier ends its uprising in 1277 (baptism), the uprising page ends the fighting in 1274. (4) Added the Swedish occupation of Braniewo, Frombork and Orneta in 1626-1635 and capital_move events for 1280 and 1306.

Not settled: (1) The Teutonic Order protectorate (1243-1464, 'a protectorate of the Monastic state of the Teutonic Knights') and the Polish overlordship (1464-1772, infobox 'part of Poland (1464-1772)') are vassal relations that belong to the overlords' dossiers: teutonic-order (vassal_start 1243, vassal_end 1464) and kingdom-of-poland / polish-lithuanian-commonwealth (vassal_start 1464, vassal_end 1772), each naming prince-bishopric-of-warmia as counterpart; they are not repeated here because the schema puts them in the overlord's ledger. (2) No territorial change 1466-1772 is on the pages opened: the Prince-Bishopric page gives 1466 (the Peace of Thorn ended Teutonic claims), 1464 (overlordship), 1467-1479 (War of the Priests, the First Treaty of Piotrków undated on the page), 1512 (Second Treaty of Piotrków, 7 December 1512) and 1525 (loss of the two thirds of the diocese in Teutonic Prussia, an ecclesiastical change, not of the secular domain); the Warmia page gives no 1479 date. So there is no ledger event for them, and the gap between 1306 and 1626 is real. (3) The founder William of Modena and the extent in 1243 beyond 'Ermland' are on no page. (4) The Deluge page does not mention Warmia, so no 1655-1660 occupation is booked for it. (5) Lidzbark page: the seat remained with the last prince-bishop until 1795; the state ends 1772.
